newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs' O'Neill touts Canadian dollar.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs' O'Neill touts Canadian dollar.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs & Co Chief Foreign Exchange Economist Jim O'Neill on Wednesday singled out Canada's currency for its particularly good value among the dollar bloc.

He said the Canadian dollar is probably the "best place to be" out of the Canadian, New Zealand and Australian currencies. O'Neill, a managing director, spoke at a Goldman, Sachs annual foreign exchange conference here.

O'Neill emphasized Canada's improving balance of payments and current account positions as reasons for his bullish view of the currency. Goldman's forecasts calls for the U.S. dollar to weaken against the Canadian dollar, eroding from C$1.35 at one month to C$1.30 in 12 months.

The economist was less sanguine on New Zealand's currency, meanwhile, calling it "extremely vulnerable." He noted the kiwi was also "overvalued," a notion also supported by some of New Zealand's own policy-makers. He sees the New Zealand dollar weakening against the U.S currency from US$0.69 in one month to $0.67 on a 12-month horizon.

O'Neill noted the yen has been greatly weakened and driven by the low level of interest rates in Japan. However, he said he finds it "pretty difficult" to simply extrapolate into the future the yen's slide will continue. O'Neill predicted "sometime in the next few months" the yen should start to reverse its trend.
